title: Reproducible Setup Example
text: This quarto markdown document (.qmd) is used to setup a reproducible environment needed to run the “Little Spectral Course” .qmd files for use in unmixing. Separately, the rendered code chunks together create a Quarto website, which can then be deployed to GitHub pages so that others can access it via an url.

title: Reproducible Setup Example
Reproducible Setup Example
text:
Dataset Retrieval
For this reproducible example, you can either provide your own .fcs files, or alternatively, use a small downsampled dataset used for the TRU-OLS/AutoSpectral walk-through in the Cytometry in R course. If you want to use the provided dataset, set the value below to “TRUE”.

RetrieveExternalDataset <- FALSE
# RetrieveExternalDataset <- TRUE


if (RetrieveExternalDataset == TRUE){

    if (!requireNamespace("httr", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("httr")
    if (!requireNamespace("jsonlite", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("jsonlite")

    library(httr)
    library(jsonlite)

    owner  <- "UMGCCCFCSR"
    repo   <- "CytometryInR"
    branch <- "main"

    FullStainedSamplesPath <- "course/community/TRU-OLS/data/samples"
    UnmixingControlPath <- "course/community/TRU-OLS/data/unmixing_controls"

    #####################
    #      Samples      #
    #####################

    SamplesFolder <- file.path(DataFolder, "samples")
    if (!dir.exists(SamplesFolder)){dir.create(SamplesFolder)}

    api_url <- sprintf(
    "https://api.github.com/repos/%s/%s/contents/%s?ref=%s",
    owner, repo, FullStainedSamplesPath, branch
    )

    resp <- GET(api_url)
    stop_for_status(resp)

    files <- fromJSON(content(resp, as = "text", encoding = "UTF-8"))

    for (i in seq_len(nrow(files))) {
    if (files$type[i] == "file") {
        dest <- file.path(SamplesFolder, files$name[i])
        download.file(files$download_url[i], destfile = dest, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
        message("Downloaded: ", files$name[i])
    }
    }

    #####################
    # Unmixing Controls #
    #####################

    UnmixingControlsFolder <- file.path(DataFolder, "unmixing_controls")
    if (!dir.exists(UnmixingControlsFolder)){dir.create(UnmixingControlsFolder)}

        api_url <- sprintf(
    "https://api.github.com/repos/%s/%s/contents/%s?ref=%s",
    owner, repo, UnmixingControlPath, branch
    )

    resp <- GET(api_url)
    stop_for_status(resp)

    files <- fromJSON(content(resp, as = "text", encoding = "UTF-8"))

    for (i in seq_len(nrow(files))) {
    if (files$type[i] == "file") {
        dest <- file.path(UnmixingControlsFolder, files$name[i])
        download.file(files$download_url[i], destfile = dest, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
        message("Downloaded: ", files$name[i])
    }
    }
}


if (RetrieveExternalDataset == FALSE){
 
    #####################
    #      Samples      #
    #####################

    SamplesFolder <- file.path(DataFolder, "samples")
    if (!dir.exists(SamplesFolder)){dir.create(SamplesFolder)}

    message("Remember to transfer your full-stained samples to the 'data/samples' folder")

    #####################
    # Unmixing Controls #
    #####################

    UnmixingControlsFolder <- file.path(DataFolder, "unmixing_controls")
    if (!dir.exists(UnmixingControlsFolder)){dir.create(UnmixingControlsFolder)}

    message("Remember to transfer your unmixing controls to the 'data/unmixing_controls' folder")

}

Remember to transfer your full-stained samples to the 'data/samples' folder


Remember to transfer your unmixing controls to the 'data/unmixing_controls' folder


At this point, within your working directory, you will have a data folder with subfolders for both samples and unmixing_controls. If you are providing your own .fcs files, please copy the corresponding raw .fcs files to their respective folders.

title: Setting Up GitHub pages
text:
If you want to share the website version on GitHub pages, there are a couple additional steps for setup after addition of the index.qmd and _quarto.yml files. First off, render the website via your terminal with the following

# In your terminal when at the working directory level, run 

quarto render

Once this is accomplished, add, commit and push your changes back to GitHub.
From there, navigate to Settings

Select Pages

Then select deploy from Branch, then the appropiate branch and docs folder.

At which point you should be set.
